conviction_note: The evidence is close to balanced. On the negative side: transpacific freight rose after the July guide, against management's stated expectation that rates would ease, with 50% contract cover and a 3-month lag; oil and diesel shocks raise domestic logistics; branded Americas lagged the category in July. On the positive side: coconut input costs are far below a year ago, Copra is consolidated from 22 July, and short interest is a crowded 14.7% of float with calls paid. p_up 49 on an abs move of 9.5 (implied 8.74, own median 7.2, raised for a guide-sensitive H2 and the crowded short) gives -0.19. The findings sum to -0.4, the same sign at a similar small size.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue about $228M: Investing.com preview 21 Oct 2026 has $228.2M and EPS $0.47 (https://in.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/vita-coco-earnings-up-next-can-growth-offset-freight-headwinds-93CH-5645800); Benzinga has $227.8M and $0.53 (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/COCO/earnings-forecasts). The revenue bar is sourced by two agreeing estimates. The EPS bar is disputed at $0.47-0.53, with Earnings Whispers at $0.51 on $205.9M revenue (https://beta.earningswhispers.com/go/w/COCO). Tradingnews on 8 Oct had $233.7M and $0.51. Company FY26 guide: net sales $790-805M, adj. EBITDA $154-161M, GM about 40% (8-K 2026-07-23). With H1 at $396M sales and $106M adj. EBITDA, the guide implies H2 of $394-409M sales and $48-55M EBITDA.
positioning_check: Short interest is 14.74% of float with 5.28 days to cover, up 26.5% month on month (MarketBeat page read 2026-10-21, https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/vita-coco-nasdaqcoco-shares-gap-up-whats-next-2026-08-20/). Tradingnews on 2026-10-08 had 5.83M shares, 10.9% of float and 5.0 DTC, unsourced (https://www.tradingnews.com/news/coco-bounces-from-over-sold-as-short-intreset-hits-10-percent-of-float). That is a crowded short. Skew is -2.39 vol points, so calls are bid over puts ('upside paid'); put/call OI is 0.06 on 2,638 total OI, a thin chain. The stock ran +24% from the 7 Oct low of $50.65 (RSI under 30 then) to $62.7: +7.1% over 5d, +8.2% over 20d, still -25% from the 52w high. No discretionary insider sales in 3 months; the only Form 4 is COO tax withholding on 2026-08-15.

findings.finding: Transpacific ocean freight to the US kept rising after the 23 July guide, against what management said on the Q2 call. CEO Roper said index spikes would fall back; contracts give about 50% cover for the rest of 2026; cost increases hit the P&L with about a 3-month lag, in Q3 and more in Q4. Drewry Shanghai-New York went from $7,598/FEU (23 Jul) to $9,507 (20 Aug), and Xeneta Far East-USEC was $10,910 on 3 Sep (+305% since 28 Feb). Q4 gross margin, and with it the FY guide, is at risk beyond the roughly 35% H2 GM the guide already implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (23 Jul): a revenue and EPS beat with a raised guide still fell 6.8%, as investors focused on an H2 EBITDA outlook below models and soft branded Americas. Q4 2025 (Feb 2026): a margin/profit miss fell 11.4%. Q1 2026: a guide raise on lower freight and tariffs rose 29.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Piper's 9 Sep $5M/quarter freight estimate, the BofA cut to $72 on 9 Oct and the 38% drawdown all reflect it. But every published freight number assumes 'rates held', and the stock has since bounced 24% to $62.7. If the market fully expected a Q4 guide cut, the stock would not have recovered most of the drawdown into the print and calls would not be bid. Management's own July assumption (rates fall back) is what the guide rests on, and the series says it did not happen.
findings.independence: Drewry WCI (separate source): Shanghai-NY $9,507 on 20 Aug, https://www.hellenicshippingnews.com/?p=1141388. Silk Chains 10 Sep (Xeneta, Hormuz closure since 28 Feb): https://www.silkchains.com.sg/blog/coconut-market-2026-review-q4-outlook/. Shares the oil shock with the domestic-logistics finding.

findings.finding: Coconut raw-material costs in Q3 2026 were far below a year earlier. Colombo nut auctions were 9.4% lower in LKR (about 18% in USD) than in Sep 2025. Philippine desiccated coconut averaged 135 c/lb against 174 a year ago. Copra millgate and farmgate prices were 'far below year-earlier levels', and coconut oil in August was 32% below the Q3 2025 average. These are a gross-margin offset to freight that the guide's 'cost inflation' framing does not mention.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 GM ex-refund was helped by 'lower finished goods costs' and the stock still fell 6.8%. Q1 2026 GM up on pricing and lower freight rose 29.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: Every preview and target cut found discusses freight and none discusses coconut input deflation. If it were priced, the 'H2 GM about 35%' narrative would carry an offset. This is a proxy: Vita Coco buys coconut water from co-packers, mostly from young or mature nuts not sold at these auctions, and the transmission to its finished-goods cost is unconfirmed.
findings.independence: Silk Chains 10 Sep 2026 (Sri Lanka nuts -18% USD YoY, CNO -32% vs Q3 2025): https://www.silkchains.com.sg/blog/coconut-market-2026-review-q4-outlook/. Mundus Agri on copra under pressure: https://www.mundus-agri.eu/news/desiccated-coconuts-copra-prices-remain-pressure.n38237.html

findings.finding: Q3 is the first quarter with Copra consolidated (closed 22 Jul 2026, $175M upfront; Copra guided calendar-2026 net sales above $100M, a cold-chain business growing 48% CAGR). It adds something like $25-30M to Q3 revenue. The street revenue bar is split: Earnings Whispers has $205.9M while Investing.com and Benzinga have about $228M, so some estimates may not carry it.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats are routine for COCO (Q2 26: $216M vs $206.7M; Q3 25: $182M vs $159M) and have been both bought (Q3 25 +7.2%) and sold (Q2 26 -6.8%). The revenue line does not reliably move the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Copra is inside the FY guide, which the company said includes it, and the main consensus of about $228M already sits roughly 25% above Q3 2025. Only the lower estimates would show a headline beat.

findings.finding: On the Q2 call (23 Jul) the CFO said Vita Coco branded was 'a little behind the category last few weeks'. He guided the category to hold in the low 20s% and said the guide implies H2 top-line deceleration ex-Copra, citing distributor builds and Walmart load-in timing. Branded Americas coconut water grew only about 14% in Q2 ($137.9M vs $120.5M), the line that sold the Q2 print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: softer branded Americas despite a total beat, -6.8%.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the company said it publicly in July. This is net of the rest of the company: private label is guided +90-100% in the US for 2026, International grew about 60% in Q2, and Copra adds. Branded Americas weakness would need to be large to dent total revenue. Kept small.
findings.independence: Q2 8-K segment table: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001482981/000162828026049279/coco-20260630xexx991pressr.htm (same company, a different document). No Q3 scanner data found.

findings.finding: Oil shock: Brent was $105.91 on 8 Oct and US diesel hit a record $6.53/gal in September. On the Q2 call management named higher domestic logistics, packaging and supplier energy costs as later-year margin pressures. Those inputs moved further after the 23 July guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 GM said domestic logistics partly offset gains and the stock fell 6.8% on the H2 outlook.
findings.why_not_priced: The 7 Oct -7% day was tied to the oil and yield rebound, so part of this is in the price. The stock has since retraced, which suggests the market is not carrying a full Q4 cost hit. This is macro-to-company transmission, confirmed only directionally by management in July.
findings.independence: Management named domestic logistics on the Q2 call: https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-vita-coco-tops-q2-2026-estimates-as-sales-jump-28-93CH-4809207. Shares the oil driver with the ocean-freight finding; the cost lines are separate.

findings.finding: Section 301 'forced-labor' duties of 12.5% have applied to the Philippines, Vietnam and Brazil (Brazil stacked on 25%) since 24 Jul 2026. Thai coconut water is reported exempt, and the exemption status of Philippine and Vietnamese coconut water (HTS 2009.90.40) is unconfirmed. In July the CEO said tariff rates had increased since the prior report.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: tariff exemptions and lower tariffs in the guide, +29.7%. Q4 2025: tariff costs in a profit miss, -11.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: Likely inside the July guide, since the regime was announced around the print date. File small. If coconut water is not exempt, Q3 COGS carries a new duty on Philippine supply that no preview mentions.
findings.independence: Bangkok Post (Thai coconut water exempt from the 12.5%): https://www.bangkokpost.com/business/general/3291215/key-thai-exports-dodge-higher-us-tariffs

findings.finding: Crowded short into a guide-sensitive print. Short interest is 14.7% of float (5.3 DTC), up 26.5% month on month. The stock has bounced 24% off an RSI-under-30 low and the chain bids calls over puts (skew -2.39). A merely in-line H2 outlook gives the squeeze mechanism room.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 +29.7% came on a guide raise; the reactions are fat-tailed (max 29.7, median 7.2).
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest was building into the print, not covering, by the MarketBeat count. Part of the 24% bounce may already be covering, which caps this.
findings.independence: Tradingnews 8 Oct, 10.9% of float, 5.0 DTC: https://www.tradingnews.com/news/coco-bounces-from-over-sold-as-short-intreset-hits-10-percent-of-float. The two short-interest figures disagree.

findings.finding: The board added $40M to the buyback on 21 Jul 2026, leaving $60.9M of capacity (the 10-Q shows $20.9M left at 30 Jun plus $40M). The stock traded $50-65 in Q3, so Q3 repurchases may lower the diluted share count, which already carries the Copra shares issued.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No history of the buyback moving the stock on a print.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is public. The Q3 execution size is unknown until the 10-Q or release, and a large Q3 buyback near the lows would read as a confidence signal.

findings.finding: Harmless Harvest, the cold-chain premium competitor, entered shelf-stable coconut water in March 2026, Vita Coco's core format. This is incremental competition in the quarters measured.
findings.why_not_priced: Known since March, and the category grew 29% YTD anyway. Tiny.

findings.finding: Supply disruption: a Philippines earthquake cost 'several weeks of production', about 1% of annual network production, as disclosed on the Q2 call, at a time of low inventory ($82.9M at 30 Jun vs $111.5M at 31 Dec, -26%).
findings.why_not_priced: Disclosed and inside the guide; the low inventory adds a small risk of Q3 shipment constraint.

outside_window.finding: PAGASA says a strong El Niño is active and could become very strong into H1 2027 (NOAA gives a 69% chance of a historic event Oct-Dec 2026). Coconut supply tightness is expected from Q4 2026, peaking Q2-Q3 2027. This is a 2027 cost risk for coconut water supply, though it may be raised on the call.

rejected_candidates.detail: Contradicted by the dated trade series (TM Duché 5 Oct, Silk Chains 10 Sep), which show copra and CNO well below a year ago.

baseline_tension: The skew (calls paid) and the crowded, building short lean up into the print, and the 24% bounce off the lows says the market is not braced for a guide cut. My freight and oil findings cut against that, but they are partly priced, so the net is near zero with a slight negative.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (crowded short at 14.7% of float, call skew): ocean-freight negative cut from -1.2 to -1.0; p_up moved from 48 to 49.

Lesson 6 (inside guide): Copra cut from +0.3 to +0.2 and Section 301 from -0.3 to -0.2, both inside the July guide. The revenue bar is sourced by two agreeing estimates (about $228M); EPS is disputed, so EPS-dependent sizing stays small.
Lesson 9 (segment net of rest): branded-Americas lag cut from -0.5 to -0.4, net of private label +90-100% and International.
Lesson 5 (proxy): coconut input deflation cut from +0.6 to +0.5; oil/diesel kept small at -0.7 -> -0.5 as macro transmission only directionally confirmed.
Positioning finding (+1.0), buyback (+0.2) and the two -0.1 items left standing.
